newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian interbank rates lower in active trade.
newsitem.headline: Croatian interbank rates lower in active trade.

text.p: The Croatian money market was busy, with supply failing to meet strong demand for kuna funds on Wednesday morning.
"Today is a deadline for corporate profit tax payments and banks expect to have large payouts," one dealer said. "This boosted demand for interbank loans."
To meet these, some creditors asked borrowers to repay previous loans and also sought funds themselves, the dealer added.
"We even called the banks which stayed out of the market today, asking if they had funds on offer," the dealer said.
Settlements rose to 63 million kuna by mid-morning, compared with a meagre 19.2 million kuna on Tuesday. Demand overshot supply by 12 million kuna.
Call money rates varied, although most loans were granted at a flat 10.5 percent.
Interbank term rates edged down slightly to 13 percent for two-week funds and to 11 and 12 percent for one week.
Overnight trade totalled 62.3 million kuna on Tuesday, mostly borrowed by two banks for mandatory reserves.
